A real difference between two official renditions; the record follows its canonical source, the export, exactly. The closing example of the statement lists three equations, each with a placeholder for the unknown number. The adopted PDF (page 23) prints a question mark as the placeholder in the first equation and an empty square box in the second and in the third; the record, like the cell of the export, has a question mark in all three. So two characters differ, the placeholders of the second and third equations. No word and no number differs, and the statement begins and ends where the record does. The script reported a match because it compares word tokens and does not see the placeholders. The export is encoded in Windows-1252, which has no box character, so its question marks at those two places are probably a substitution made by the export: an importer or export matter, not something to fix in the pack's text. The Summary shows all three placeholders as question marks, following the export; its meaning is not affected, and In a child's hands already speaks of an empty box. Cluster heading right; Limits right.

Round 2. The wording is the export's as corrected from the adopted document at two places (at each, a symbol the export had lost is restored). It now equals the page image (PDF page 23, number 8, the last statement under the last cluster heading of the domain, two lines, directly above the bar of the next domain): in the closing example the unknown of the first equation is a question mark and the unknowns of the second and of the third equation are empty square boxes; numbers, signs and order are equal, and the statement starts and ends where the record does. Compared by eye: the script's token match holds at this place but does not see the three placeholders, and the PDF's text layer holds the box as a private-use glyph, so the page image is what settles it. The minus sign is an en dash in the PDF and a hyphen in the record: form. Cluster heading right. Summary judged again: faithful (one unknown, addition or subtraction, three whole numbers; the three examples kept as examples, each with its numbers right and the position of its unknown named correctly) and of the pack's own shape (the examples are regrouped by the role of the unknown and given in another order). It writes the placeholder as a question mark in all three examples, where the wording now has a box in two: notation only, no number or position changes, but it could be brought in line with the corrected wording. Limits right: neither the statement nor its heading sets a range, the examples stay within 12, and other statements of the domain work within 20. The two wrong answers under Common mistakes are worked correctly from the examples.

Round 3. Confirmed in round 2; two changes since. (1) The Summary now writes the unknown as an empty box in two of its three examples and as a question mark in one, each in the equation where the stored wording and the page have it (checked example by example against the page image, PDF page 23). (2) Limits has one new sentence saying that the stored wording is the export's as corrected from the adopted document at two places. That is what the importer's list holds for this code (two corrections, each restoring a box the export had lost), and both are right on the page image: the unknown of the first equation is a question mark, those of the second and of the third are empty square boxes. The PDF's text layer holds the box as a private-use glyph, so the image settles it; the script's token match holds at this place but does not see the placeholders. The minus sign is an en dash in the PDF and a hyphen in the record: form. Read whole: Summary faithful (one unknown, addition or subtraction, three whole numbers; the three examples kept as examples, their numbers right, the role of the unknown named rightly in each) and in the pack's own shape (the examples regrouped by role and given in another order). Limits right: no number range in the statement or in its heading, the examples stay within 12, neighbouring statements work within 20. The two wrong answers under Common mistakes are worked rightly (19; 2). The statement is number 8, the last under the last cluster heading of the domain; it starts and ends where the record does. Cluster heading right.
